insights.topic: Verified purchase proof vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: Crinkl's cryptographic receipt verification converts purchase confirmation into a deterministic signal — a structural contrast to the probabilistic inference that underpins most cookieless targeting alternatives. At $2.17M beta GMV across 37,576+ confirmed receipts, the dataset is no longer a proof-of-concept sample.

insights.topic: Category mix shift toward grocery and dining
insights.insight: Grocery-supermarkets (1,312 receipts, ~$61 avg basket) and restaurants-dining (1,147 receipts, ~$39 avg basket) now lead volume in the 14-day window, compressing the overall average from ~$80 to ~$65 — a category mix effect, not a demand softness signal. For CPG and QSR brands, this is the relevant audience composition.

insights.topic: Walmart, Costco, Target dominate verified brand share
insights.insight: Walmart holds 369 receipts, Costco 177, and Target 128 in the trailing 14-day window — the three retailers accounting for the bulk of identifiable brand volume. For competing brands or suppliers to these retailers, this is a verified share-of-wallet benchmark, not a modeled estimate.

insights.topic: Home improvement emerging as a concurrent category signal
insights.insight: The Home Depot (67 receipts) and Lowe's both appear in the current top brand list simultaneously — the first instance of two home improvement brands crossing the visibility threshold in the same heartbeat sequence. Brands targeting homeowners or home-adjacent purchase occasions should note this as an early category signal.

insights.topic: Digital and subscription commerce verified alongside physical retail
insights.insight: YouTube's confirmed presence in the top brand list, alongside a DKIM vendor set that includes Amazon, OpenAI, Stripe, Paddle, and Gumroad, establishes that receipt verification extends across physical retail, digital goods, and SaaS — a single verified identity graph spanning channel types that cookieless solutions typically treat as separate.

insights.topic: High-value unclassified spend warrants category resolution
insights.insight: The 'Unknown' category carries a ~$336 average basket — approximately 5.5x the grocery average — across 217 receipts in the 14-day window. Until these receipts are classified, a meaningful share of the highest-value verified transactions in the dataset remains unmapped to any targetable category.
